current_answer: People have built games, browser demos, desktop apps, art, brain engines and research tests on real fruit fly connectomes, mainly FlyWire (female brain) and MaleCNS (male brain and nerve cord). We checked 100 of them on 1 October 2026: 36 can be opened in a browser or free notebook without installing anything. Most viral demos really run a simulated fly brain, but a person chose which neurons receive the input and which neurons act, and several get most of their movement from scripts or trained parts; the Half-Life demo does not load a connectome at all by default, and DesktopFly mostly switches coded animations. No fly has been "uploaded". The week's most-viewed fly-brain claim, "I Taught a Fly How to Play Gorilla Tag (seriously)" (527,756 views on 1 Oct 2026), names no model, data or code and is graded U, like a Roblox fight video (139,364 views), the Pokémon-on-a-Raspberry-Pi stream and the Rainbow Six Siege claim. Does the real fly wiring help? Sometimes: real fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 10 of 24 studies, mostly reflex, sensory and steering circuits; in trained, reservoir and ML tasks it tied or lost (7). The answer depends on how the wiring is scrambled: in our own pre-registered test of the sugar reflex (one model, one trial per shuffle), degree-preserving and weight shuffles silenced the feeding motor neuron MN9 (0 Hz against 85.2 Hz, 5 shuffles each), scrambling only the interior wiring kept 46% (39 Hz), and sign shuffles made the whole brain fire (214 Hz with about 3.6 million spikes). A degree-preserving shuffle made up to 1.7 times more active than the real brain still gave 0 Hz, but no gain matched the real activity, so by our fixed rules our own study row scores mixed, with an unfair null and weak method. Even where wiring helps, a brainless baseline often matches the fly: in Doom the fly survives 53.34 s, shuffled wiring 6.75 s and a brainless autopilot 51.93 s (the best of 12 autopilot settings 53.44 s), and across 14 studies with a no-brain baseline the fly network beats it in only 2. Only 9 of 32 control studies are methodologically strong, the other numbers are the authors' own and none is replicated. A beginner can run the published whole-brain model on a CPU: in our test on 2 CPUs (Linux, 28 minutes) sugar input drove MN9 to 85.2 Hz, and shuffled wiring dropped it to 0 Hz; a re-test on 1 Oct 2026 gave the same pins, checksums and tests and 82.0 Hz bit-exact.

catalogue_card.question: What have people built with the digital fruit fly brain, and what is real?
catalogue_card.text: 100 fruit fly brain simulation projects checked in code: 36 you can try online, 51 demo and lab videos with evidence grades, verdicts on 19 viral claims, 32 control studies, and our own pre-registered test that scrambles the fly brain four ways.

summary: 100 entries checked on 1 Oct 2026 (6 new in the fifth check): 21 grade A, 19 B, 23 C, 4 D, 9 U and 24 datasets or tools (not graded).

Our own fair test (made by us, pre-registered on 1 Oct 2026 before any scrambled trial): on the sugar reflex of the Shiu et al. whole-brain model, real wiring gives MN9 85.2 ± 3.56 Hz (5 trials; re-runs bit-exact). Degree-preserving shuffles 0 ± 0 Hz and weight shuffles 0 ± 0 Hz (5 each): silent. Boundary-preserving (interior-only) shuffles 39 ± 1.22 Hz (retention 0.46): partly. Sign shuffles 214 ± 43 Hz, but only because the whole brain ignites (about 3.6 million spikes, about 60,500 active neurons): runaway.

Gain check of the fair test: a degree-preserving shuffle with synapses 1.5, 2 and 3 times stronger stayed at 0 Hz even when the brain was 1.7 times more active than real, but no gain came within ±30% of the real activity, so by the pre-registered rule the arm is not matched. Limits: one reflex, one model, one trial per shuffle, MN9 rate cannot tell selective drive from global ignition, gain arm on one shuffle.

By our fixed ledger rules our own study row now scores mixed, with an unfair null and weak method (30 Sep: helps, partly fair, moderate): without a matched gain the nulls are not 'tuned equally', and on the MN9 metric the sign-shuffle runaway counts as the null doing better. We did not override the rules.

Does fly wiring help? Sometimes: real fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 10 of 24 studies, mostly reflex, sensory and steering circuits; in trained, reservoir and ML tasks it tied or lost (7). Of 32 control studies, 24 have a wiring null: helps 10, no difference 5, worse 2, mixed 6, not yet scored 1. Reflex circuits: helps 3, mixed 1 (our own test).

Where the wiring helps, a brain-free baseline often matches the fly anyway: the fly network beats a no-brain baseline in only 2 of 14 studies. In Doom (doom-fly-control, results/a2/summary.json at commit 6b22922), the fly survives 53.34 s, shuffled wiring 6.75 s (3 seeds), a brainless autopilot matched to the fly's average commands 51.93 s, and the best of 12 autopilot settings 53.44 s. New: Brain Runners, 82.34 rows real vs 27.84 shuffled vs 74.05 with no brain.

"I Taught a Fly How to Play Gorilla Tag (seriously)" (SuperCatCrazeGT, wK4lixw7p4M; 527,756 views on 1 Oct 2026): grade U. No model, data or code is named; the only link is a linktr.ee page; four GitHub searches found nothing. The video was not watched, so on-screen claims are not recorded. "I Made Two Real Flies Brain Fight Each other in JJS" (139,364 views): grade U, no code.

The choice of null changes answers: in flyconnectome-nulls standard nulls beat the connectome (1.78 and 1.77 vs 1.57) but nulls that keep the sensory-motor boundary tie it (1.58 and 1.62); in our own test, four nulls give silent, partly and runaway. A fair control keeps degrees and signs, tunes the null like the real wiring, uses 3 or more shuffles with a spread, reports activity next to the readout, and includes a no-brain baseline.

FlyLeno (Vinesauce stream, 42,125 views on 1 Oct 2026): grade B, borderline C. The whole FlyWire v783 brain runs live and untrained in the browser, but inputs and outputs are hand-mapped, gait, homing and the choice of actions are engineered, and there is no control.
Pokémon on a Raspberry Pi 5 and the Rainbow Six Siege fly brain: both still grade U after a re-check on 1 Oct 2026; no code has appeared.

36 entries have a no-install link (one is a live stream); all answered our HTTP check on 1 Oct 2026, but none was played by us. FlyDoom (eganeganegan) returned HTTP 404 on 1 Oct 2026; its record is kept until a re-check.

In viral demos a real connectome usually runs, but people chose the input and output neurons; DesktopFly, FlyCraft, Bad Apple, FlyDrones, the FlyBridge Minecraft farming demo and the Roblox maze race get much of their visible behaviour from scripts, stimulus, training or a synthetic network, and the Half-Life demo (grade D) builds a synthetic network by default although its videos claim MaleCNS v1.0 and "no scripted game AI".

Video gallery (1 Oct 2026): 51 videos, 45 of them original uploads by the project's author, lab or institution or by the creator of the claim, plus one streamer's playthrough (FlyLeno); 33 of 100 catalogue entries have at least one video.
"91%" is the share of 164 testable predictions of the brain-only Shiu et al. 2024 model that matched experiments; "95%" compares versions of the model and is not an accuracy.
FlyWire data is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); MaleCNS, MANC, hemibrain and BANC data are CC BY.

Build your own, tested 28 Sep 2026 and re-tested from an empty folder on 1 Oct 2026 on Linux with 2 CPUs and no GPU: pins and data checksums unchanged, 6 of 6 tests passed, first sugar trial 82.0 Hz bit-exact with the first run; the Shiu et al. model on FlyWire v783 gave MN9 85.2 Hz with sugar input at 150 Hz and 0 Hz on shuffled wiring. A new box, Try a fair control yourself, gives our weight- and sign-shuffle code; wiring it into the beginner files is untested. Adding a FlyGym body needs Python 3.12 to 3.14; brain-body coupling is untested by us.
uncertainty: Our fair test covers one reflex (sugar to MN9) in one model (Shiu et al. leaky integrate-and-fire, upstream parameters), with one 1 s trial per shuffle at one trial seed and 5 shuffles per arm. The MN9 rate cannot tell selective drive from global ignition. The gain check ran on one shuffle and matched no gain; the optional matched-gain and extra-shuffle trials were not reached. The boundary split depends on FlyWire's cell-class annotation.

No demo was played in a real browser; "page responds" is an HTTP check only. The Gorilla Tag and Roblox fight verdicts rest on watch-page metadata only (the videos were not watched); about half of the watch-page view counts were refused (HTTP 429).

Controls ledger: every number except our own test is the authors'. We recomputed 15 studies from their committed files and spot-checked 8 a second time, but re-ran none; none is replicated, and only 2 of 32 are peer-reviewed. Only 9 of 32 studies reach "strong" method quality; 18 are weak.

Ledger labels (wiring effect, fairness, quality) come from fixed yes/no rules applied to code and files; they are consistent but coarse. Our own study is "mixed" by rule although its arms read silent, partly and runaway. One label (Fly.exe, mixed) was set by hand. Retention puts very different measurements on one scale and shows direction and size, not significance. The flyvis ablation values sit in a figure and were not extracted. fly-cartpole's ledger numbers are from an earlier commit; its new numbers (392.5 vs 390.3 steps) give the same verdict but rest on a protocol we have not read.

The "helps" results are mostly one kind of test (does a reflex pathway still carry signal after rewiring?), which is a low bar; boundary-preserving nulls have now been applied to one reflex (ours: 46% kept), not to the other reflex studies.

Borderline grades: FlyLeno (B, borderline C); Fly Worker, fly-brain by Lulzx, The Fly's Hash Function, Fly OCR, Fly Self Driving, the null-model study and fly-brain-zero-shot are borderline A; fly-brain by erojas and Kick the Fly could argue B; acamilo-flybrain would sit on the B/C border without its stream macros.

Several C grades and the fafbseg entry rest on file citations that we spot-read but did not re-verify line by line. fly-plays-games runs its neurons in an external package (fly.ai) that we did not inspect.

The Pokémon stream and the Rainbow Six claim are known only through news articles, a Reddit post and a Twitch page read through summarising tools or search summaries; X, TikTok and Reddit cannot be searched without a login.
Stars, creation and last-push dates of some records were reused from earlier checks and are labelled with those dates in projects.json.

Not yet triaged: a research project with its own controls and several new low-star repositories (not opened in time), leads deferred in earlier weeks, a FlyGym derivative with a BANC bridge (deferred to the next check, not linked), and about 211 repositories listed only in directories.
Why the Shiu v783 file has 616 fewer neurons than the FlyWire v783 release is not established; the scope of BANC's "approximately 188,000 neurons" is not stated.

The Build your own guide is untested on macOS, Windows/WSL, Colab and machines with a C++ compiler; GitHub Pages publishing is untested. The 1 Oct re-test did not re-run the full 20-trial demo or the change-one-thing experiments. DOOMFLY's and DesktopFly's run steps are untested by us.
FlyWire data licence conflict: CC BY-NC 4.0 in the official guidelines vs CC BY 4.0 on the Zenodo v783 record; we follow the stricter, non-commercial reading.
Video summaries rest on titles, descriptions, captions, code and thumbnails; we did not watch every video frame by frame. View counts are snapshots.

Videos cannot play inside the site: YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok and X players failed in the site's sandboxed frames (tested in headless Chromium only). YouTube and X thumbnails are loaded from their image servers.
